question.:question/worked-solution:

$$

By contrast, matrices $A$, $B$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry below the diagonal:

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -4 \\ 10 & 6\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}-11 & -3 & -2 \\ -6 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 8\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
D=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 10 & -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
E=\begin{bmatrix}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 2 & 8 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.
